common_name: Ambassador White Begonia (Green-Leaf Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost using fine seed sown on the surface of moist starting mix, then transplant outdoors once frost danger has passed.

directions: Ambassador White is the pure-white-flowered member of Sakata's early-blooming Ambassador series, carrying glossy true-green foliage on a dense, uniform mound rather than the bronze leaf color found in darker-leaved wax begonia lines. It reaches flowering size faster in the pack than many older green-leaf strains, giving growers an earlier finish for spring bedding sales, and continues blooming steadily through summer heat once planted out. Pair it with Ambassador Scarlet or Rose for a crisp color contrast in mass plantings, and keep soil evenly moist for the cleanest, most continuous flower display.
sources: Sakata Ornamentals — Ambassador series variety page
Ball Horticultural Company product listing: Begonia Ambassador White

common_name: Ambassador Pink Begonia (Green-Leaf Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost on a heat mat under bright light, then transplant into well-drained bedding soil once frost danger has passed.

directions: Ambassador Pink bears soft, clear pink flowers with a yellow-stamened center over glossy green foliage, offering a gentler color option within the same early-flowering, heavily basal-branched Ambassador series as Ambassador Scarlet. The compact, mounded habit resists stretching in the pack and holds its shape in the landscape through the growing season. It performs well in beds receiving morning-to-midday sun and tolerates summer humidity without significant foliage decline. Deadheading is unnecessary since spent blooms are self-cleaning.
sources: Sakata Ornamentals — Ambassador series variety page
Garden Center Marketing plant listing: Begonia semperflorens Ambassador Soft Pink

common_name: Ambassador Rose Begonia (Green-Leaf Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost using fine pelleted seed, then transplant outdoors once nights stay reliably above freezing.

directions: Ambassador Rose produces deeper rose-pink flowers than its Pink sibling, held above glossy true-green foliage on the same compact, vigorous mound bred for early, uniform flowering across the Ambassador series. It holds up well in beds and mixed containers where consistent color from spring through fall is the goal, tolerating both humid heat and the intermittent afternoon shade common in mixed borders. Feed lightly through the season to sustain flower production, and keep the root zone evenly moist rather than letting it dry between waterings.
sources: Sakata Ornamentals — Ambassador series variety page
Garden Center Marketing plant listing: Begonia semperflorens Ambassador Rose

common_name: Ambassador Bicolor Begonia (Green-Leaf Bicolor Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost under bright light, then transplant into moist, well-drained bedding soil after all frost danger has passed.

directions: Ambassador Bicolor stands out from its solid-colored Ambassador siblings with flowers combining white and rose-pink tones on the same bloom, set against the series' characteristic glossy green foliage and dense, early-flowering mound. The two-tone effect reads as a lively accent when mixed with solid Ambassador colors in beds or window boxes rather than planted alone in large blocks. Like the rest of the series it branches heavily from the base without pinching and keeps flowering through summer heat with only routine watering and light feeding.
sources: Sakata Ornamentals — Ambassador series variety page
NC Farms Inc. wholesale plug listing: Begonia Ambassador Bicolor

common_name: Cocktail Rum Begonia (Bronze-Leaf Bicolor Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Sow dust-fine seed on the surface of moist, sterile starting mix under bright light without covering, then transplant outdoors after frost danger has fully passed.

directions: Rum is the bicolor member of the Cocktail series, its white-and-rose-red flowers standing out sharply against the same dark bronze-maroon foliage shared by Gin, Vodka, and Whiskey. The tight, compact mound needs no deadheading and blooms continuously from spring through the first hard frost, and its bronze leaf pigment lets it handle brighter light than green-leaved wax begonias without scorching. Use it in mixed containers or as a bedding accent where its two-tone flowers add contrast alongside the series' solid-colored siblings.
sources: Benary — Begonia semperflorens F1 Cocktail Rum product page
Park Seed product listing: Cocktail Rum Begonia Seeds

common_name: Cocktail Brandy Begonia (Bronze-Leaf Pink Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Sow fine seed on the surface of moist, sterile starting mix under bright light, then transplant into well-drained soil once frost danger has passed.

directions: Brandy carries clear pink flowers in loose clusters over the thick, waxy, dark bronze foliage typical of the Cocktail series, filling out into the same compact, mounding habit as its Gin, Vodka, Whiskey, and Rum siblings. It blooms heavily and continuously from planting through frost without deadheading, and the dark leaf color tolerates more direct sun than green-leaved wax begonias while still performing well in partial shade. Space plants for airflow to keep foliage dry and reduce disease pressure in humid climates.
sources: Benary — Begonia semperflorens F1 Cocktail Brandy product page
Park Seed product listing: Cocktail Brandy Begonia Seeds

common_name: Prelude Rose Begonia (Compact Early-Flowering Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost, since fine begonia seed needs many weeks to size up, then transplant outdoors once frost danger has passed.

directions: Prelude Rose produces clusters of rose-pink flowers over compact green foliage on one of the earliest-flowering wax begonia strains available, reaching bloom in the pack noticeably sooner than many older bedding lines. Its exceptionally uniform, low mound stands up well to both heavy rain and summer heat, making large-scale plantings look tidy with little maintenance. It works well massed in beds or used as an edging plant, and needs only routine watering and light feeding to bloom continuously into fall.
sources: Ball Seed Company product listing: Prelude Rose Begonia
PanAmerican Seed plant introductions

common_name: Prelude White Begonia (Compact Early-Flowering Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost under bright light, then transplant into well-drained bedding soil after frost danger has passed.

directions: Prelude White bears clean white flowers over compact, uniform green foliage, sharing the same early-to-flower habit that distinguishes the Prelude series from slower bedding begonia lines. The dense, low mound resists flopping in rain and holds its form through a full season of heat and humidity. It brightens shaded borders and mixed containers when paired with the series' pink, rose, or scarlet colors, and requires only consistent moisture and light monthly feeding to stay in continuous bloom.
sources: Ball Seed Company product listing: Prelude Mix Begonia
PanAmerican Seed plant introductions

common_name: Prelude Pink Begonia (Compact Early-Flowering Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost, then transplant into moist, well-drained soil once frost danger has passed.

directions: Prelude Pink carries soft pink blooms over tidy green foliage on the same fast-flowering, compact frame shared across the Prelude series, giving growers an early finish and gardeners a long season of bloom. The tight mound stays neat without pinching and tolerates both rain and summer heat better than many older semperflorens strains. It works well massed in beds, window boxes, or as edging, needing only regular water and modest fertility to bloom from spring through the first frost.
sources: Ball Seed Company product listing: Prelude Pink Begonia

common_name: Prelude Scarlet Begonia (Compact Early-Flowering Bedding Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost under bright light, then transplant outdoors after all frost danger has passed.

directions: Prelude Scarlet delivers the brightest color in the series, its vivid scarlet-red flowers set against compact, uniform green foliage on the same early-blooming, weather-tough mound as its Prelude siblings. It reaches flowering size ahead of many older bedding begonias, giving a fuller look at planting time, and continues blooming steadily through the heat and humidity of a full summer. Use it for bold mass-planted color in beds or containers, watering consistently and feeding lightly to keep flower production high.

common_name: Doublet White Begonia (Double-Flowered Bronze-Green Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start seed or root cuttings indoors well ahead of the last frost, then transplant into moist, well-drained soil after frost danger has passed.

directions: Doublet White is the white-flowered selection in Danziger's double-flowered Doublet series, its frilly, rose-like blooms opening in clusters over glossy dark green foliage tinted with coppery bronze. The fully double flowers give a fuller, more ornamental look than single-flowered wax begonias while retaining the same self-cleaning habit, so spent blooms drop cleanly without deadheading. It performs from full shade into considerable sun as long as moisture stays consistent, and suits hanging baskets, patio containers, and garden beds alike.
sources: Danziger — Doublet series product page
Emerisa Gardens plant listing: Begonia 'Doublet White'

common_name: Doublet Pink Begonia (Double-Flowered Bronze-Green Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start seed or root cuttings indoors ahead of the last frost, then transplant outdoors into well-drained soil once frost danger has passed.

directions: Doublet Pink produces frilly, light pink double flowers resembling miniature roses over dark green, bronze-tinted foliage, giving the Doublet series its distinctive fuller bloom compared to standard single-flowered wax begonias. The compact, mounding plant tolerates conditions from shade to considerable sun and blooms from mid-spring through mid-fall without needing deadheading. It is well suited to hanging baskets and patio containers as well as garden beds, requiring only steady moisture and routine feeding to stay in continuous flower.
sources: Danziger — Doublet Pink product page
Peace Tree Farm plant listing: Begonia semperflorens Doublet series

common_name: Doublet Red Begonia (Double-Flowered Bronze-Green Wax Begonia)

planting.note: Start seed or root cuttings indoors ahead of the last frost, then transplant outdoors after all frost danger has passed.

directions: Doublet Red bears dainty, frilly red double flowers at the stem tips from mid-spring to mid-fall, set against broad, heart-shaped, dark bronze-green foliage with burgundy tints characteristic of the Doublet series. Its fully double blooms give a rose-like fullness rarely seen in wax begonias, and the plant is self-cleaning, dropping spent flowers without deadheading to keep beds looking tidy all season. It handles conditions from shade to considerable sun and heat, performing well in hanging baskets, patio containers, and mixed garden beds alike.

common_name: Super Olympia Red Begonia (Early-Flowering Green-Leaf Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost under bright light, then transplant into well-drained landscape or bedding soil once frost danger has passed.

directions: Super Olympia Red bears clusters of small, rich red, orchid-like flowers with bright yellow centers over glossy green foliage on a uniform, early-flowering landscape strain that has performed especially well in deep South regional trials. The compact plants tolerate partial sun to full sun without stretching and hold up to summer heat and humidity better than many older green-leaf wax begonias. It is well suited to large-scale bedding displays where dependable, weather-tough color is the priority, needing only routine watering and light feeding through the season.
sources: Benary — Begonia semperflorens F1 Super Olympia Red product page
University of Florida IFAS Extension

common_name: Super Olympia Pink Begonia (Early-Flowering Green-Leaf Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost, then transplant into well-drained soil after frost danger has passed.

directions: Super Olympia Pink carries clusters of light pink, orchid-shaped flowers with yellow centers over bright green foliage, part of an early-flowering, heat-tolerant landscape series that has proven especially reliable in deep South regional trials. Plants stay compact and uniform from partial sun into full sun exposure, resisting the stretch and flower fade seen in older bedding begonia lines during peak summer heat. Use it for mass color in beds or containers, watering consistently and feeding lightly for continuous bloom into fall.

University of Florida IFAS Extension

common_name: Super Olympia Rose Begonia (Early-Flowering Green-Leaf Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost under bright light, then transplant into well-drained soil once frost danger has passed.

directions: Super Olympia Rose produces small, rose-pink, orchid-like flowers with contrasting yellow centers over compact green foliage on the same early-blooming landscape strain that has stood out in deep South heat trials. The uniform, well-branched habit fills beds quickly and keeps flowering through the most humid stretches of summer with minimal care. It tolerates a wide range of light from partial to full sun, making it a flexible choice for mixed borders, edging, or large mass plantings.

common_name: Super Olympia Bicolor Begonia (Early-Flowering Green-Leaf Bicolor Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Start indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost, then transplant into well-drained soil after frost danger has passed.

directions: Super Olympia Bicolor combines white and rose-pink tones on each small, orchid-shaped flower, setting it apart from the solid-colored members of the Super Olympia series while sharing the same compact green foliage and dense, early, uniform flowering habit. Bred as part of a landscape strain noted for strong performance in deep South heat trials, it holds up to summer humidity and continues flowering with minimal deadheading. Mix it with solid Super Olympia colors for two-tone bedding displays, or use it alone as an accent in containers and borders.
